decisions.reason: As a close-to-core carpet in a growing furniture market, it likely stays unless its early sales fall below aspiration, though the firm's broad range makes a similar decorative rug relatively easy to prune.

This hand-knotted wool silk carpet fits the firm's premium craftsmanship positioning, so with no visible sign of underperformance and some industry slack, management would more likely retain it while results remain uncertain.

Because it is another close-to-established low-pile decorative carpet, boundedly rational management would usually keep it absent clear failure, but overlap with other rugs raises the chance of later portfolio trimming.

The corner bench builds directly on the firm's established furniture offer and workplace/living concepts, so it is more likely to meet aspiration and be kept than a more easily substitutable accessory item.

A low-pile carpet is close to the existing assortment and cheap to test, yet among several similar rug launches it faces the highest risk of being dropped if it does not quickly justify its place in the portfolio.

The swivel shell chair is a natural extension of the firm's seating and flexible workplace focus, so in a growing industry management would usually keep it unless 2024 performance clearly falls short of aspiration.
